name: Google Waltham Cross data centre
summary: Google data centre on a 33-acre site in Waltham Cross, Hertfordshire, England. Google announced a $1 billion investment in the new facility in January 2024, describing air-based cooling with provision for off-site heat recovery to nearby homes and businesses. Chancellor Rachel Reeves opened the data centre in September 2025, when Google also announced a two-year GBP 5 billion UK investment covering capital spending, R&D and engineering. Google says the site supports AI services, Google Cloud, Search and Maps. Power capacity has not been disclosed.

location.note: Town centroid of Waltham Cross via Nominatim; Google's sources name the town but not the street address.

milestones.note: Opening by the Chancellor reported in Google's post of this date.

power_sources.description: Google's 2022 offshore wind PPA with ENGIE for the Moray West farm in Scotland, adding 100 MW to the grid, covers its UK operations rather than this site alone.
Shell manages Google's UK carbon-free energy portfolio and is to deploy battery technology that stores surplus clean energy for the grid; the arrangement is UK-wide, not specific to this site.

notes: The GBP 5 billion figure announced at the opening is a two-year UK-wide programme covering capital spending, R&D and engineering, including Google DeepMind research, so it is not recorded as a campus investment. Google's location page says the facility uses air cooling that limits water use to domestic needs.
